text:
maya: incident-bot just paged oncall for token-router — spike in 5xxs and p99 latency. paging now. @chris @taylor please ack
incident-bot: PAGE triggered by rule: token-router/error-rate > 1% over 2m AND p99_latency > 700ms; incidents/1749072000 created. links: https://infra/alerts/1749072000
chris: acked. looking at logs + traces. I see a config push at 13:02 that touched kv-cache sharding.
ops-bot: deploy metric: deploy/token-router/2025-03-12-1302 succeeded (duration 97s)
taylor: jumping in — grabbing flamegraphs and tailing gateway logs
eli: routing note: a few enterprise tenants reported broken responses to /v1/generate, ~30 requests failing per min
chris: initial tail: stacktraces show NPE in hash-router when shard list empty on retry path. likely a race on startup config update.
maya: customer-impact summary: multiple paid customers saw errors; some got 504s from our edge. CS already triaged two tickets.
taylor: mitigations tried: 1) rolled forward a hotfix that adds guard for empty shard list; 2) toggled routing fallback to safe-mode (force local routing)
chris: after hotfix, 5xx rate dropped from 6.3% -> 0.8% in 4m. p99 latency back to ~420ms. rolling metrics attached: 
```
before: error_rate=6.3%, p99=1120ms
after: error_rate=0.8%, p99=420ms
```
eli: verified ingress traces show normal throughput; no backlog in request queues now.
maya: good. is this safe to close page or should we keep monitoring?
taylor: keep open for a bit. I’ll take on-call handoff at 1749072300, will monitor for 30m then close.
chris: agree. also need a follow-up: reduce noise from this alert and update routing policy — it's paging for >1% across entire fleet, which made some non-customer-impact changes noisy.
maya: filing post-incident action items now. proposal thread below for alert tuning and routing changes.
maya: PROPOSAL: split severity based on customer impact and affected endpoints. high-level idea:
```
severity_policy: |
  critical: page (immediate) when - multi-customer SLA-affecting errors OR ingestion/produce endpoints down
  major: page (oncall) when - single-high-value-customer > 5% errors for 5m OR >3 customers impacted
  minor: ticket to #eng-sre when - noisy non-customer-facing errors or infra warnings
```
chris: +1. concrete rules recommended: change current rule from error_rate >1% across all to:
```
rule token-router/error-critical:
  when: (error_rate > 1% AND affected_customers >= 2) OR (p99 > 1000ms AND error_rate > 0.5%)
  severity: critical
  route: page -> pagerduty -> eng-oncall channel mapping
rule token-router/error-major:
  when: (error_rate > 1% AND affected_customers == 1 AND customer_tier == enterprise) OR (spike > 3x baseline)
  severity: major
  route: page -> oncall (if after-hours) else ticket -> #eng-sre
rule token-router/noise:
  when: error_rate between 0.2% and 1% AND affected_customers == 0
  severity: minor
  route: ticket -> #eng-sre
```
eli: suggest adding an automatic suppression for deploy windows: if deploys in last 5m, throttle pages to a ticket with high priority tag, unless multi-customer errors detected. reduces tedious wakeups during rollouts.
maya: agree — add "deploy-aware suppressions" to alert manager. ops-bot, can you add a flag to annotate alerts with recent_deploy=true when applicable?
ops-bot: noted — will add alert annotation "recent_deploy" if deploy token-router occurred in previous 5m; will default to suppressed escalation if only minor. PR to follow.
taylor: next items: 1) create dashboard filter by customer (latency/error by customer) 2) add runbook section: "how to decide page vs ticket" with checklist 3) update oncall rotation doc with new channel mappings
chris: I'll own the dashboard (svc/token-router -> by-customer panels) and the updated alert rules PR. aiming for a config PR by EOD.
maya: I'll own runbook edits and coordinate with support on customer comms templates.
eli: I'll add the deploy-aware suppression RFC to infra tickets and own implementation with ops-bot.
maya: handoff: taylor taking monitoring watch until 1749072420 then hand back to normal rotation. quick summary to include in postmortem: cause=shard-list race on config apply; mitigation=hotfix guard + safe-mode routing; customer-impact=select enterprise tenants saw 5xx/504s for ~8m; followups=alert routing policy, deploy-aware suppression, dashboard by-customer, runbook update.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED at 1749072420. incident/1749072000 closed.
chris: will link the PRs and postmortem once complete. thanks team. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks all, great response. we should meet for 15m post-incident sync tomorrow.
